feasibility_reasoning: The one product-code edit cannot work. In .output/server/_tanstack-start-manifest_v-DcVEtS0X.mjs, routes["/"].preloads = [index-BHIMq0Mj.js, blog.index, headings, Footnotes, PaginatedPostGrid, useInFeedAds, prepareContent, eventInvoiceMath]. That is the / route chunk plus its static imports: .output/public/assets/index-BHIMq0Mj.js has plain `from"./Footnotes-…"`, `from"./PaginatedPostGrid-…"`, `from"./blog.index-…"`, `from"./headings-…"`, `from"./prepareContent-…"` and `from"./useInFeedAds-…"`. The router loads the route chunk before hydration, so these chunks are fetched no matter what. TanStack also writes them as <link rel=modulepreload> in <head> (scratchpad/psi/home.html). Filtering them out of the Link header in src/lib/http/frameworkPreloads.server.ts:14-28 therefore changes only linkHeaderEntries/preloadDuplicates. Taking them out of the head as well would create an import waterfall (+1 RTT before hydration). admin.analytics is not in the HEAD artifact's root preloads (the entry index-DPN2YAij imports only vendor chunks); it appears only in the older prod deploy. The gate half is feasible as pure code but overstated. (a) document-weight-budgets.json already holds preloadedJsGzipBytes {max 572985, measured 561750, target 153600}, so the listed budget change is a no-op. `target` never gates (documentWeight.ts Budget.target), and ratchetBudgets=min(old,new) cannot move toward the target without the byte cuts. (b) check-document-weight.ts, documentWeight.ts and the budgets file are untracked (git status ??). No package.json script or CI workflow runs them, and the gate needs build:smoke plus the fixture backend. first-visit.yml:52-59 already builds and could host it, so the effort is M rather than S. (c) A 'brotli' preLcpTransferBytes does not match the gzip-only weigh() (gzipSync). assetName() matches only js|css, so the woff2 fonts in /assets are missed. The hero variant depends on viewport/DPR, and the fixture hero is a 113 KB JPEG on a separate origin. A static sum cannot see Lantern's runtime set (requests ended before observed LCP, about 130 KB more of the post-boot wave on PSI). There is no SSR/i18n/SEO/CLS risk.

effect_reasoning: The gate itself saves 0 ms; it only prevents regressions. Upper bound for the stray drop, from batch1.out P_stray (requests deleted entirely, which the real change does not do): mobile FCP 3974→3973, LCP 4819→4743 (−76 ms), perf 65→65; desktop FCP −41, perf 99→99. The real change keeps those fetches, so its effect is ≈0. The claimed slope is high: M_bytes_all (≈300 KB) measures FCP −1351 / LCP −1426, i.e. 4.5 / 4.75 ms/KB, not 5 / 6. FCP is not byte-uniform: CSS −49 KB gives 0 ms FCP, while JS gives about 4.3 ms/KB. Single what-ifs sum to −1.8 s LCP against −1.43 s combined, so they are not additive. PSI with score.py: now 3100/6600/600/4900 → 53. Byte diet alone with TBT unchanged, 1750/5170/600/4300 → 63; with TBT +200 ms from window coupling (LA-F4) → 58. W1 only (TBT 150) → 66. W1 + diet → 76. So the diet's increment is about +7–10 pts on top of W1, and it belongs to boot-js/css/html-weight. The 85 depends on the unverified PSI FCP→LCP gap collapse (LA-F8). Desktop: −0.08 s per 100 KB is 0 pts at fixture 99 and about +1 on PSI (LCP 1.1 s).
corrected_estimate: LA-C3 as specified: 0 pts mobile and desktop (the gate is a guard rail; the stray-header drop is ≤−76 ms LCP even with the requests fully removed, ≈0 in practice). Byte diet credited to its owners: ≈4.75 ms/KB LCP and 4.5 ms/KB FCP (JS only); −300 KB gives fixture 65→83, PSI 53→63 without W1 (58 if TBT coupling adds 200 ms) and 66→76 with W1. Cheaper and better: (1) add preLcpTransferBytes as a gzip derived sum of the existing htmlGzip + renderBlockingCssGzip + preloadedJsGzip + woff2 preloads + 768w hero, and run check-document-weight in first-visit.yml; (2) add a runtime gate in lighthouse.yml from the LH JSON (analyze.py: KB of High requests ended before obs LCP), which is the set Lantern actually scores; (3) drop the frameworkPreloads edit and remove the ≈8 KB gzip of route-closure chunks through lazy imports or a chunk-graph fix.
better_alternative: Make the gate a gzip derived sum of the fields the document-weight gate already measures, and run it in first-visit.yml (which already builds build:smoke). Add a runtime LH-JSON gate on the KB of High requests that ended before the observed LCP. Remove the stray chunks by lazy-importing Footnotes, PaginatedPostGrid and similar components in the / route, not by filtering the Link header.
